transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since my daughter left for basic training, I’ve been a mess. I come home and the house just feels dead. I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts, and at work I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I’ve snapped at some of the younger guys too. I don’t go out on the water anymore or work on my sculpture. I just... don’t see the point right now.
How long ago did your daughter leave for basic training, and how long have you been feeling this way since then?
It’s been about a month since she left. I’ve been struggling pretty much since then.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep since your daughter left—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my sleep lately.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed whether my appetite or weight has changed.
Have you been feeling worthless, or blaming yourself for things, more than usual since this started?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I’ve been blaming myself or feeling worthless.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low in energy, even after resting?
I can’t really say. I haven’t noticed whether my energy’s been different or not.
Would you say you feel down or find yourself not caring about things almost all day, every day, or does it come and go depending on the day?
It’s pretty much every day since she left. I come home and the house just feels dead, and I don’t really care about doing the things I used to. I just… don’t see the point sometimes.
When you say you 'don't see the point' sometimes, have you had any thoughts of death or of harming yourself?
I’m not sure. I mean, I feel like things are pointless sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about death or hurting myself.
Have you noticed any new difficulty concentrating or making decisions since your daughter left, aside from the missed steps at work?
Yeah. I keep losing my place doing things I’ve done for years, and it’s like I can’t settle my mind long enough to make a simple decision.
Have your coworkers or family mentioned that you seem to be moving, talking, or reacting more slowly than usual—or conversely, that you seem more restless or fidgety than before?
I’m not really sure. Nobody’s said anything to me about moving or talking differently.
Do you feel this low and down all the time now, even when you're distracted or busy with other things, or does it mainly come on when something reminds you of your daughter being gone?
It mostly hits me when I get home and the house is empty, or something reminds me she’s gone. At work I can stay busy for a while, but even then it’s kind of sitting there underneath.
